sources.title: Flood risk and coastal change
sources.role: MHCLG planning practice guidance for flood risk and coastal change.
sources.facts: Current England planning guidance covers flood sources, sequential and exception tests, site-specific assessment, SuDS and coastal change.
sources.origin: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.
sources.guard: Planning guidance is not a site-specific flood-risk assessment, flood-depth measurement, sequential-test decision or permission.

sources.title: National flood risk standing advice for local planning authorities
sources.role: Environment Agency standing advice for application screening and consultation.
sources.facts: Published 15 April 2015; updated 28 May 2026; covers development classes, FRAs, SuDS information and consultation triggers.
sources.guard: Standing advice does not prove a submitted FRA is adequate, a site is safe, or permits and consents have been obtained.

sources.title: National standards for sustainable drainage systems
sources.role: Defra national non-statutory SuDS standards publication.
sources.facts: Published 19 June 2025; updated 30 July 2025; supports design, maintenance and operation of surface-water drainage systems in England.
sources.origin: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs.
sources.guard: National standards do not prove a specific drainage design is approved, constructed, adopted, maintained or performing.

sources.title: National standards for sustainable drainage systems (SuDS)
sources.role: Detailed Defra standards for SuDS design, adoption and maintenance.
sources.facts: Sets standards and adoption responsibilities for surface-water systems, including systems serving more than one property.
sources.origin: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs.
sources.guard: Standards and adoption routes do not prove an asset has been accepted, vested, maintained or compliant over its lifetime.

sources.title: Shoreline management plans
sources.role: Environment Agency guidance and explorer for coastal management approaches.
sources.facts: Published 30 January 2024; describes 20 English SMPs, management approaches and the national coastal erosion risk map.
sources.guard: An SMP policy unit or erosion projection does not guarantee funding, defence delivery, property protection or planning permission.

sources.title: Flood risk management plans: responsibilities
sources.role: Government guidance on EA and LLFA responsibilities for FRMPs.
sources.facts: Explains responsibilities for main-river, sea, reservoir, surface-water, ordinary-watercourse and groundwater risk planning.
sources.origin: Environment Agency and Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs.
sources.guard: A risk-management plan is strategic and does not establish exact-site risk, completed works or investment commitment.

sources.title: Surface water management plan technical guidance
sources.role: Defra technical framework for local surface-water management planning.
sources.facts: Published 10 June 2011; supports local authorities coordinating and leading local flood-risk management activities.
sources.origin: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs.
sources.guard: Technical planning guidance does not prove a local plan is current, funded, implemented or adequate for a parcel.

sources.title: Flood and coastal erosion: risk management authorities
sources.role: Official collection describing risk-management authority roles and guidance.
sources.facts: Covers lead local flood authority powers, strategies, consenting and supporting flood/coastal guidance.
sources.origin: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs and Environment Agency.
sources.guard: Authority roles and collections do not prove that a consent was issued, a structure designated, or a project delivered.
